entries.title: How can dry earth become a wall?
entries.answer: Builders can mix earth with water and shape it into adobe bricks. The bricks dry in the air and sun before people place them in a wall. A thick wall can slow the movement of heat into a room, which can be useful in a place that is hot in the day. Builders protect the outside with roof edges or layers they can repair because too much water can soften the earth again. Adobe traditions continue in many places.
facts: Dry adobe bricks can be protected with a layer of earth-based plaster.

entries.title: How could Gothic builders make room for tall windows?
entries.answer: Medieval Gothic builders used pointed arches, ribs along ceilings, and strong supports outside some high walls. Together, these features helped carry the weight of the stone and reduce some of the pressure on parts of the wall. Builders could put large windows in more places. Pieces of colored glass let sunlight make different patterns during the day. The outside supports and inside stone ribs are still easy to see in many Gothic churches and cathedrals today.
facts: Gothic builders often used stone supports called flying buttresses outside tall buildings.

entries.title: How did builders fit a huge crowd into the Colosseum?
entries.answer: Rome’s Colosseum was an oval arena with rows of seats rising around the central floor. Visitors entered through many ground-level openings. Stairways and paths led up to seating areas, making it possible for people to reach different parts of the building. Arches helped support the upper levels. Ancient Romans went there for public shows, including contests. The building changed after the Roman Empire’s ancient shows ended, and people later used some of the spaces under the seats for other things.
facts: The Colosseum is also known as the Flavian Amphitheater.

entries.title: How did Inca builders use a steep mountain ridge?
entries.answer: Machu Picchu is an Inca site high in the Andes of present-day Peru. Its builders made terraces to create level strips of land on steep slopes. Stairs connected buildings and paths at different heights. Carefully fitted stones form many of the walls. Water could follow channels rather than simply running wherever the rain took it. From far away, the buildings seem to match the outline of the ridge. Builders worked with the mountain’s shape as they made space to live and work.
facts: Machu Picchu was built during the height of the Inca Empire in the fifteenth century.

entries.title: How did older cities start to build skyscrapers?
entries.answer: In a building with heavy stone walls, the walls near the ground can become very thick as more floors are added. Builders in the late 1800s began giving tall buildings strong frames made of metal. A frame could carry more of the weight directly to the ground. That helped leave more room for windows and indoor space. Elevators also made it practical for people to reach many upper floors. Together these changes let cities fit more working space onto a piece of land.
facts: Chicago’s Home Insurance Building was an influential early tall building that opened in the 1880s.

entries.title: How did people build the city of Mohenjo-daro?
entries.answer: Mohenjo-daro was an ancient city in the Indus region of what is now Pakistan. Builders arranged many houses along streets and lanes. They used bricks made from clay, and some homes had washing spaces linked to drains. One large public building contains a basin that archaeologists call the Great Bath. Because the city’s signs have not been read with agreement, we do not know what people called the building or exactly how they used it.
facts: The ruins of Mohenjo-daro are near the Indus River.

entries.title: How does Hagia Sophia hold up its great dome?
entries.answer: Hagia Sophia is a historic building in Istanbul. Its builders had to fit a curved dome above a room with a square central space. Four broad arches and curved sections between them helped form a round base above the square. Visitors can see a ring of windows under the dome. The building opened as a church in the sixth century, then later served as a mosque and a museum. It is used as a mosque today.
facts: The present building dates from the rule of the Byzantine emperor Justinian, although parts were repaired or rebuilt later.

entries.title: What can the buildings at Chichén Itzá tell us?
entries.answer: Chichén Itzá was a major city in the northern Yucatán region, in what is now Mexico. Builders raised a stepped temple often called El Castillo. They also made a large court where a ball game could be played. Other buildings had columns, carved animals, and signs. Some parts look like buildings elsewhere in the region, while others show ideas connected with places farther away. The buildings let us compare where people met, what they built, and which ideas they shared.
facts: A natural water-filled opening called the Sacred Cenote lies near the main buildings.

entries.title: What did people build at Tikal?
entries.answer: Tikal was a large Maya city within the forest of what is now northern Guatemala. Its builders set steep temples and other large buildings around open squares. Stone stairs climbed above the trees. Away from the biggest buildings, people also built homes and worked the land. Centuries later, forest covered parts of the city. Archaeologists use buildings, pieces of pottery, and carved records to study Tikal as a place where people lived as well as a place where leaders held ceremonies.
facts: Tikal National Park now protects both the ancient site and part of the surrounding forest.

entries.title: What do the stone walls at Great Zimbabwe tell us?
entries.answer: Great Zimbabwe was an important city in southern Africa several centuries ago. Skilled builders stacked carefully fitted stone in thick walls. Curved passages and spaces inside the walls show how they shaped pathways and rooms without a simple square plan. Archaeologists also found goods made far away. Those finds show that the city took part in trade networks reaching beyond southern Africa. The standing walls and the small objects together tell a richer story than either alone.
facts: The large stone enclosure was built without mortar holding the blocks together.

entries.title: What makes the design of Angkor Wat unusual?
entries.answer: Angkor Wat is a large Khmer temple in Cambodia. A wide water-filled moat surrounds its grounds. From the main path, visitors can see stone towers rising above several levels of covered walkways. Long carvings on the walls tell stories in pictures. Its builders once dedicated it as a Hindu temple, and it later became a Buddhist place of worship. The temple is part of a much bigger historic landscape that includes roads, water systems, and remains of other buildings.
facts: Angkor Wat was built in the twelfth century under King Suryavarman II.

entries.title: What was Persepolis built to show?
entries.answer: Persepolis was a royal center in ancient Persia. Its builders made a huge level platform along a mountainside. They raised stone columns above it and decorated stairs with lines of carved figures. The figures carry items or wear clothes that mark different places. Visitors once climbed real stairs beside the carved people climbing in orderly rows. The setting, size, and art helped show the power of the Persian kings and the many lands they claimed as part of their empire.
facts: King Darius I began constructing Persepolis late in the sixth century BCE.

entries.title: Why did builders carve buildings into cliffs at Petra?
entries.answer: Petra was a trading city of the Nabataeans in what is now Jordan. Tall sandstone cliffs surrounded it. In some places, builders carved fronts and rooms directly into the rock instead of setting blocks on top of one another. Traders reached the city along routes connecting lands across dry country. To make it possible to live there, people collected and carried water in carefully built channels and storage places. The rock buildings and waterways give different clues about the same city.
facts: A narrow passage between high rock walls leads into Petra.

entries.title: Why did people build the Great Wall of China?
entries.answer: Rulers in different periods built walls, gates, and towers along parts of China’s northern frontier. Walls could slow a raid and guide people toward guarded crossings. The first Qin emperor joined some earlier defenses, but builders changed and extended walls over many centuries. Some well-known brick and stone stretches were built under the Ming. Other sections used packed earth. Looking at the Great Wall today is like looking at many building projects from different times in one landscape.
facts: The Great Wall includes branches and separate sections built in different places and periods.

entries.title: Why do some Buddhist towers have stacked roofs?
entries.answer: A pagoda is a tower found in parts of Asia. In many examples, each level has a wide roof or ledge that makes the tower look like a stack. Pagodas can be made of stone, wood, or brick, and the shape changes from place to place. Many were built in connection with Buddhism. A pagoda may mark a special place or hold objects important to worship. Some are mostly solid inside, even if the outside looks as if it has rooms on every level.
facts: Sculptures of small pagodas can help historians study building shapes that changed over time.

entries.title: Why does a flying buttress look like a bridge beside a wall?
entries.answer: A tall stone ceiling can push sideways on its walls as well as down. A flying buttress carries some of that sideways push away from the upper wall across an open space to a strong stone support. From a distance it looks like a short bridge to nowhere, but its job is to help hold the building steady. Often the space beneath it leaves room for paths or windows, while the broad support sends the forces down into the ground.
facts: A flying buttress connects an upper wall to a support farther away from the wall.

entries.title: Why was the Taj Mahal built?
entries.answer: The Mughal ruler Shah Jahan had the Taj Mahal built in Agra, India, to honor his wife Mumtaz Mahal after she died. It includes a tomb, gardens, waterways, and several other structures. The large white marble building sits at one end of the garden. Its dome stands above walls decorated with stone patterns and writing. A long pool can reflect the building along a central line. These choices help visitors see how the parts of the design fit together.
facts: The Taj Mahal was built in the 1600s in Agra.
